extracted.intended_audience: journalists, newsroom editors, journalism students, and the informed public
extracted.subtask_description: A set of core principles and responsibilities that define good journalism and what the public should expect from news organizations. The page lists chapter/section headings from Bill Kovach's 'The Elements of Journalism', each articulating a distinct journalistic standard or role.

rubrics_metrics.name: What is journalism for?
rubrics_metrics.description: Chapter/section asking and clarifying the purpose of journalism — what journalism exists to do for society and the public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Truth: the first and most confusing principle
rubrics_metrics.description: Asserts that truth is journalism's primary principle, while acknowledging complexities and tensions in how truth is pursued and presented.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who journalists work for
rubrics_metrics.description: Defines the audience and constituency journalists serve (the public) and discusses issues of loyalty, accountability, and whose interests journalism should represent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Journalism of verification
rubrics_metrics.description: Emphasizes verification as the central practice of journalism — methods and standards used to check facts, sources, and claims before publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independence from faction
rubrics_metrics.description: Stresses the need for journalists and news organizations to maintain independence from political, commercial, and ideological factions to preserve credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitor power and offer voice to the voiceless
rubrics_metrics.description: Positions journalism as a watchdog over powerful institutions while also amplifying marginalized or underrepresented voices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Journalism as a public forum
rubrics_metrics.description: Frames journalism's role in facilitating public discourse by providing a space for discussion, debate, and exchange of information relevant to civic life.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engagement and relevance
rubrics_metrics.description: Calls for journalism to engage audiences and ensure coverage is relevant to the lives and concerns of the public it serves.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make the news comprehensive and proportional
rubrics_metrics.description: Advocates for news coverage that is thorough and proportional — giving appropriate attention relative to importance and context rather than sensationalizing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Journalists have a responsibility to conscience
rubrics_metrics.description: Asserts that journalists must exercise ethical judgment and moral responsibility in their reporting and professional decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: The rights and responsibilities of citizens
rubrics_metrics.description: Addresses the reciprocal duties between journalism and citizens: citizens' rights to information and their responsibilities in a democratic information ecosystem.
